In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new instrument, the My Class Inventory, which is designed to measure the classroom environment.

the validation of the My Class Inventory, a 30-item instrument designed to measure the classroom environment in terms of five dimensions: student-teacher relations, task orientation, classroom management, instructional support, and student autonomy.
the validation of a classroom environment scale, the My Class Inventory, by means of LISREL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the empirical structure of the My Class Inventory is not well defined.
the LISREL approach provides a useful tool for testing the structure of instruments in a wide variety of contexts.
the My Class Inventory is a good measure of classroom environment, but not in the way it was originally conceptualized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LISREL is useful for the empirical testing of instruments, but that the results of these tests should be interpreted with caution.
, while the My Class Inventory has some problems, the instrument is not without merit.
, in the case of the My Class Inventory, the instrument is not a good one for measuring what it purports to measure.

the LISREL approach is an effective way of testing the structure of an instrument.
